name: Bill Shankly
scopeNote: Liverpool spell only (user decision 2026-10-12). Style named by sources as 'pass and move' (short passing, five-a-side based, very high fitness and work rate), with a '3-3-4' attacking wing-half plan in the early 1960s (Shankly's own 1962 column) and a shift after the Red Star Belgrade defeat (Nov 1973) toward patient build-up from the back. Winger-based width (Callaghan, Thompson). No source mined states zonal vs man marking; a 1964 Revie scouting dossier describes Yeats sticking 'like glue' to the centre-forward and full-backs staying close to wingers, which suggests individual marking but is not labelled as such. Appointment date 1959-12-01 is from the brief; Empire of the Kop says confirmed 14 Dec 1959 (not verified against a second source). Dates for generic style facts are given as '1959-74' because sources do not date them.
openQuestions: Zonal vs man marking is not stated by any mined source (gap). The 1964 Revie dossier (full-backs 'keep close to the wingers', Yeats 'sticks like glue to the centre-forward') hints at man-oriented marking, only an inference.
Appointment date: brief says 1959-12-01, Empire of the Kop says 14 Dec 1959 confirmed; the latter may be the announcement date. Check a second tier A-B source.
Tommy Smith quote (never practised corners/set-pieces) is relayed by Tomkins and Empire of the Kop, no primary interview found.

Red Star 1973 as the turning point is from Tomkins/Wilson retrospectives; Shankly publicly praised Red Star but said fans would not pay to watch it. How much was the Boot Room (Paisley) rather than Shankly is contested (Tomkins credits the Boot Room).
Pressing is documented only as high work rate/fitness and 'work twice as hard to get it back', not as a high-line pressing system; no tier A source found.

Tomkins notes Shankly was sentimental with older players (Paisley was ruthless), but Empire of the Kop says Shankly phased out Liddell and others early; the 1965-66 Shankly quote says he set age limits for players.

statedView.quote: Our approach was to use the ball like a baton in a relay race. You pass it to me, I pass it to him, he passes it on. It’s the ball that is covering most of the ground — not the players.
Never pass to a red shirt in one direction when there are two in the other... Support the man, but look to the ball. If you lose the ball work twice as hard as the opposition to get it back.
Tae get the best out of his men, the manager has tae work tae a tactical plan they understand which need not necessarily be the one he'd like himself.
If I don't pick the team, what am I manager of?
We realised at Liverpool that you can’t score a goal every time you get the ball. And we learned this from Europe, from the Latin people.
We don’t have eleven players here, we have twenty.
My idea was to turn Liverpool into a bastion of invincibility.
Don’t think any individual is expected to win the game by himself. Don’t worry that we are depending on you too much. Share out the worries.
